passages.original: namque huius opera hostes, cum castra iam intrassent, multis milibus regiorum interfectis profligati sunt exercitusque reliquus conservatus regis est: qua ex re maioribus rebus praeesse coepit. erat eo tempore Thuys dynastes Paphlagoniae, antiquo genere, ortus a Pylaemene illo, quem Homerus Troico bello a Patroclo interfectum ait. is regi dicto audiens non erat. quam ob causam bello eum persequi constituit eique rei praefecit Datamen, propinquum Paphlagonis: namque ex fratre et sorore erant nati. quam ob causam Datames primum experiri voluit, ut sine armis propinquum ad officium reduceret.
passages.english: For it was through his efforts that the enemy, when they had already entered the camp, were routed after many thousands of the king's men had been killed, and the rest of the king's army was saved; as a result of this he began to be put in charge of greater affairs. At that time Thuys was ruler of Paphlagonia, a man of ancient lineage, descended from that Pylaemenes whom Homer says was killed by Patroclus in the Trojan War. He was not obedient to the king. For this reason [the king] resolved to make war on him, and put Datames, a kinsman of the Paphlagonian, in charge of the matter, for they were the sons of a brother and a sister. For this reason Datames wanted first to try to bring his kinsman back to his duty without arms.
passages.notes: 'Dynastes' (a local hereditary ruler) is rendered 'ruler'. The subject of 'constituit' (resolved) is the king, implied from 'regi'.
